messages.content:
You are an experienced UK building control surveyor. Answer the question about the work item
in the JSON state. Choose exactly one label:
- not_notifiable: No Building Regulations notice needed: not building work (reg 3), only Schedule 4 work, or an exempt building (reg 9, Schedule 2).
- competent_person_scheme: Notifiable work listed in Schedule 3: a registered competent person can self-certify it (reg 12(6)(a)); otherwise a building notice is needed.
- building_notice_or_full_plans: Building work not covered by Schedules 3 or 4: a building notice or a full plans application to building control (reg 12(2)).
- full_plans_required: Building work that must have a full plans application: the Fire Safety Order applies to the building (reg 12(3)), it fronts a private street (12(4)), or H4 applies (building over or near a sewer, 12(5)).
Reply with JSON only: {"label": "<one label>", "probabilities": {"<label>": <0..1>, ...}} with a
probability for every label, summing to 1.

Under the Building Regulations 2010 in England, which notification route applies to this work item if it is carried out on its own in the building described?

{"work_item": "Opening up two adjoining shop units into one with a new steel beam", "project": "Retail units in England", "jurisdiction": "England. The Building Regulations 2010 as amended.", "clauses": [{"ref": "reg 12(6A)", "document": "BR2010", "text": "(6A) A person intending to carry out building work in relation to which Part P of Schedule 1 imposes a requirement is required to give a building notice or an application for building control approval with full plans where the work consists of— (a) the installation of a new circuit; (b) the replacement of a consumer unit; or (c) any addition or alteration to existing circuits in a special location."}, {"ref": "para 2.8", "document": "ADP2013", "text": "2.8 Installing fixed electrical equipment is within the scope of Part P, even if the final connection is by a standard 13A plug and socket, but is notifiable only if it involves work set out in regulation 12(6A). For example: a. installing a built-in cooker is not notifiable work unless a new cooker circuit is needed b. connecting an electric gate or garage door to an existing isolator switch is not notifiable work, but installing a new circuit from the consumer unit to the isolator is notifiable. Building Regulations 2010 Application of Part P"}, {"ref": "para 2.2", "document": "ADP2013", "text": "2.2 Part P applies to electrical installations: a. in a dwelling-house or flat, and to parts of the installation that are: (i) outside the dwelling – for example fixed lighting and air conditioning units attached to outside walls, photovoltaic panels on roofs, and fixed lighting and pond pumps in gardens (ii) in outbuildings such as sheds, detached garages and domestic greenhouses. b. in the common access areas of blocks of flats such as corridors and staircases c. in shared amenities of blocks of flats such as laundries, kitchens and gymnasiums d. in business premises (other than agricultural buildings) connected to the same meter as the electrical installation in a dwelling – for example shops and public houses below flats."}]}

message.reasoning: Since these are shop units with a steel beam alteration, this is a structural change under Part A plus fire safety under Part B, and since they're non-domestic, the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order applies — meaning full plans are required under reg 12(3) rather than a building notice. The Part P references are just distractors here since that's for domestic electrical work.
